title: How property, football and politics link Manchester and Abu Dhabi

evidence_packet.title: How property, football and politics link Manchester and Abu Dhabi
evidence_packet.lead: A closer look at the relationship between Man City's owners and the Manchester political scene
evidence_packet.summary: A closer look at the relationship between Man City's owners and the Manchester political scene
evidence_packet.evidence_text: When Manchester City was found guilty in September of breaching Premier League financial rules, the damning and unprecedented verdict left the football world reeling An independent commission said the club had "systematically" broken rules between 2009 and 2018 by inflating sponsorship revenue to disguise secret funding of more than £830m into its football operations Speculation is now rife about the level of punishment City will face, although the club denies any wrongdoing and has appealed against the ruling While we await the outcome, the historical relationship between City's Abu Dhabi-based owners and Manchester's political elite - including the now Prime Minister Andy Burnham - has been in the spotlight There has been a focus on land deals, multimillion-pound regeneration schemes, and more recently, investigations into loans handed out to property companies owned ultimately by City's owner, the Abu Dhabi United Group (ADUG) Beyond the on-field success at the Eithad Stadium, what exactly is the Abu Dhabi story in Manchester?

title: Salford man's journey from brain injury to stand-up comedy

evidence_packet.title: Salford man's journey from brain injury to stand-up comedy
evidence_packet.lead: Ben Shelvin was once told he would never talk or walk ever again but found a unique way to bounce back
evidence_packet.summary: Ben Shelvin was once told he would never talk or walk ever again but found a unique way to bounce back
evidence_packet.evidence_text: A man who was once told he might never walk or talk again following a devastating brain injury says stand-up comedy has become the key to his recovery Ben Shelvin was hospitalised after a drunk driver crashed into his moped during a family holiday to Croatia back in 2003 Now aged 44, Shelvin, from Salford, has made a near complete recovery, and has gone on to carve out a career performing stand-up comedy, and even run half-marathons He described the road to recovery as "a long process" but said the best advice he had to offer was to "just keep going" Born in 1982, Shelvin said his childhood was very active, and filled with all kinds of sport, including football, athletics, and cricket He went on to study at Manchester Metropolitan University, and the day after his graduation flew out to Dubrovnik in Croatia for a two-week family holiday

title: The case against each man accused of abusing woman drugged by husband

evidence_packet.title: The case against each man accused of abusing woman drugged by husband
evidence_packet.lead: The prosecution has been outlining its case against nine men accused of abusing an unconscious woman
evidence_packet.summary: The prosecution has been outlining its case against nine men accused of abusing an unconscious woman
evidence_packet.evidence_text: This past week prosecutors have been outlining their case against a group of nine men - including a paramedic, children's football coach and taxi driver - who allegedly raped or abused a woman after she had been drugged by her husband The husband, who cannot be named to protect his wife's legal right to anonymity, had already pleaded guilty to 62 offences against her committed at the home they shared in the Stockport area of Greater Manchester Four other men have also admitted sexual offences against her, but the remaining defendants deny all charges and are on trial at Manchester Minshull Street Crown Court Louise Oakley KC, lead counsel for the prosecution, has told the jury that both the husband and the other men were leading "double lives" while secretly fulfilling their "barbaric fantasies" The husband's own abuse against the woman, in her sixties, is believed to have begun in 2004 before he began inviting strangers he met on online chatrooms, swinging websites and messaging apps to join him from about 2023 Here the BBC summarises the allegations against each man standing trial

title: Ex-Macclesfield FC co-owner's relief after investigation dropped

evidence_packet.title: Ex-Macclesfield FC co-owner's relief after investigation dropped
evidence_packet.lead: Robert Smethurst was released without further action after a thorough investigation, Cheshire Police says
evidence_packet.summary: Robert Smethurst was released without further action after a thorough investigation, Cheshire Police says
evidence_packet.evidence_text: An investigation into a former Macclesfield FC boss has been dropped, police have confirmed Robert Smethurst was arrested in Wilmslow, Cheshire, on 19 May on suspicion of controlling and coercive behaviour Cheshire Police said the former co-owner of the National League North club had since been released without further action "due to insufficient evidence" following "a thorough investigation" Smethurst said: "Of course I am relieved but I knew 100% that I was not guilty." The 48-year-old bought the club out of insolvency in 2020 and installed former manager Robbie Savage Under his leadership, the club secured a FA Cup giant killing win last season after beating holders and Premier League side Crystal Palace 2-1

title: Memorial lit up for first time in a century as part of North West Remembrance tributes

evidence_packet.title: Memorial lit up for first time in a century as part of North West Remembrance tributes
evidence_packet.lead: The spectacle is just one of the many colourful tributes for Remembrance Day across north-west England
evidence_packet.summary: The spectacle is just one of the many colourful tributes for Remembrance Day across north-west England
evidence_packet.evidence_text: A neglected war memorial has been painstakingly restored by volunteers and lit up for the first time in its 104-year history ahead of Remembrance Day The Grade II* listed Hoylake and West Kirby monument has been transformed thanks to 14 years of renovations by the Friends of Grange Hill and Wirral Borough Council The spectacle is just one of a range of colourful tributes and events ahead of Remembrance Sunday across north-west England They include a striking display of thousands of poppies and crosses on a roundabout in Leigh, Greater Manchester, while Poulton-le-Fylde in Lancashire, has a displayed more than a 1,000 yellow poppies to honour "forgotten heroines" who served their country The Hoylake and West Kirby restoration project began in 2012 after a visitor tried to bring his father, a military veteran, to the memorial but found access virtually impossible Years of neglect had left the site overgrown while the site's remembrance garden had almost disappeared

title: Johnny Marr guitar could fetch £30k at Wiltshire auction

evidence_packet.title: Johnny Marr guitar could fetch £30k at Wiltshire auction
evidence_packet.lead: The Fender American Vintage 1962 Reissue Stratocaster was played during Marr's time with British rock band The The
evidence_packet.summary: The Fender American Vintage 1962 Reissue Stratocaster was played during Marr's time with British rock band The The
evidence_packet.evidence_text: A guitar used by Johnny Marr after his split from The Smiths could fetch up to £30,000 when it goes under the hammer next month The white Fender American Vintage 1962 Reissue Stratocaster was played during Marr's time with British rock band The The which he joined in 1988, a year after leaving The Smiths Auctioneers Gardiner Houlgate said a private owner bought the guitar in 2020, with Marr - originally from Manchester - signing the guitar's headstock at the time and providing a handwritten postcard describing how it had been used The guitar will go on sale at the Gardiner Houlgate auction house in Corsham, Wiltshire, on 8 December where it is estimated to fetch between £20,000 and £30,000 Luke Hobbs, auctioneer at Gardiner Houlgate, said: "We're valuing this guitar at around £20,000 to £30,000 based on other recent sales of Johnny Marr's instruments "Marr's equipment is very popular with collectors and fans

title: Thousands to celebrate Diwali across the North West

evidence_packet.title: Thousands to celebrate Diwali across the North West
evidence_packet.lead: Worshippers are marking the Hindu Diwali festival in temples across the region
evidence_packet.summary: Worshippers are marking the Hindu Diwali festival in temples across the region
evidence_packet.evidence_text: Thousands of people are preparing to enjoy food, music and fireworks as Hindus across north-west England are set to celebrate Diwali About 600 are expected for the festival at the Gujarat Hindu Society in Preston, Lancashire, on Sunday, which opens with prayers and features a fireworks display finale Ishwer Tailor, vice president of the temple, which celebrated its 50th anniversary last year, said it had been planning the events for a month He said Diwali was a "fun" celebration where people come together at the temple throughout the day with the "spectacle" of the shrine decorated with lamps "and plenty of sweets for everyone" Diwali, or the Festival of Lights, is a five-day Hindu festival celebrated by Hindus, Sikhs, and Jains It takes its name because houses, shops and public places are decorated with small oil lamps called diyas

title: Raped wife learned of 20 years of abuse after husband's arrest, trial hears

evidence_packet.title: Raped wife learned of 20 years of abuse after husband's arrest, trial hears
evidence_packet.lead: Nine men are accused of taking part in or facilitating the abuse of a woman at her husband's invitation
evidence_packet.summary: Nine men are accused of taking part in or facilitating the abuse of a woman at her husband's invitation
evidence_packet.evidence_text: Warning: This article contains distressing content A woman who was drugged and raped by her husband for 20 years was first told she may have been the victim of sexual offences shortly after his arrest, a court has heard Prosecutors said a knock on the door of the couple's home in Stockport, Greater Manchester, in October 2025 was the moment "the life she knew ended" The husband, who has pleaded guilty to rape, was arrested after an international investigation was prompted by undercover journalists in Germany infiltrating a Telegram group used by people interested in sex with someone who was asleep or unconscious The investigation identified the husband, who was in his 60s, as a user who had shared images showing the sexual abuse of his wife Nine men are on trial at Manchester Minshull Street Crown Court accused of various offences involving the woman's abuse

title: Third person charged over stabbing death

evidence_packet.title: Third person charged over stabbing death
evidence_packet.lead: Adrian Brown was found with stab wounds to the chest on Raby Street in Moss Side on 8 May
evidence_packet.summary: Adrian Brown was found with stab wounds to the chest on Raby Street in Moss Side on 8 May
evidence_packet.evidence_text: A third person has been charged in connection with the fatal stabbing of a father of three in Manchester, police said Adrian Brown, 34, died in hospital after being found with stab wounds to the chest on Raby Street in Moss Side on 8 May Emeil Lee, 26, currently of HMP Forest Bank, has been charged with murder as part of the investigation into Brown's death. He is due to appear before Manchester and Salford Magistrates' Court on Monday Greater Manchester Police (GMP) said a 17-year-old boy had previously been charged with murder, while Taio Lee, 18, had been charged with attempted Section 47 assault Police appealed for anyone with information to come forward Tell us which stories we should cover in Greater Manchester

title: Wigan veteran finds permanent home after 20 years in motorhomes

evidence_packet.title: Wigan veteran finds permanent home after 20 years in motorhomes
evidence_packet.lead: James Makinson says a housing scheme has given him security after decades spent living on the road
evidence_packet.summary: James Makinson says a housing scheme has given him security after decades spent living on the road
evidence_packet.evidence_text: After spending more than 20 years living in caravans and motorhomes, army veteran James Makinson said having a permanent home gave him one thing: "security" Known as Jimmy, the 79-year-old was helped into accommodation in Wigan through Homes at Ease, a housing programme run by the not-for-profit organisation Armed Forces Community HQ The scheme helps veterans who are homeless or at risk of losing their homes find permanent accommodation through social housing providers and private landlords. Since 2023, it has received more than 500 referrals across the North West "I can't say enough about this place," Makinson said of Armed Forces Community HQ, which helped him Lisa Murgatroyd, strategic development director at the organisation, said 99.5% of veterans housed through the scheme remained in permanent accommodation for more than six months Murgatroyd said much of the homelessness experienced by veterans was hidden, with people staying on friends' sofas or in insecure accommodation rather than sleeping rough

evidence_packet.evidence_text: When Manchester City was found guilty in September of breaching Premier League financial rules, the damning and unprecedented verdict left the football world reeling An independent commission said the club had "systematically" broken rules between 2009 and 2018 by inflating sponsorship revenue to disguise secret funding of more than £830m into its football operations Speculation is now rife about the level of punishment City will face, although the club denies any wrongdoing and has appealed against the ruling While we await the outcome, the historical relationship between City's Abu Dhabi-based owners and Manchester's political elite - including the now Prime Minister Andy Burnham - has been in the spotlight There has been a focus on land deals, multimillion-pound regeneration schemes, and more recently, investigations into loans handed out to property companies owned ultimately by City's owner, the Abu Dhabi United Group (ADUG) Beyond the on-field success at the Eithad Stadium, what exactly is the Abu Dhabi story in Manchester?

evidence_packet.evidence_text: This past week prosecutors have been outlining their case against a group of nine men - including a paramedic, children's football coach and taxi driver - who allegedly raped or abused a woman after she had been drugged by her husband The husband, who cannot be named to protect his wife's legal right to anonymity, had already pleaded guilty to 62 offences against her committed at the home they shared in the Stockport area of Greater Manchester Four other men have also admitted sexual offences against her, but the remaining defendants deny all charges and are on trial at Manchester Minshull Street Crown Court Louise Oakley KC, lead counsel for the prosecution, has told the jury that both the husband and the other men were leading "double lives" while secretly fulfilling their "barbaric fantasies" The husband's own abuse against the woman, in her sixties, is believed to have begun in 2004 before he began inviting strangers he met on online chatrooms, swinging websites and messaging apps to join him from about 2023 Here the BBC summarises the allegations against each man standing trial

title: Memorial lit up for first time in a century as part of North West Remembrance tributes

evidence_packet.title: Memorial lit up for first time in a century as part of North West Remembrance tributes
evidence_packet.lead: A neglected war memorial has been painstakingly restored by volunteers and lit up for the first time in its 104-year history ahead of Remembrance Day The Grade II* listed Hoylake and West Kirby monument has been transformed thanks to 14 years of renovations by the Friends of Gran
evidence_packet.summary: A neglected war memorial has been painstakingly restored by volunteers and lit up for the first time in its 104-year history ahead of Remembrance Day The Grade II* listed Hoylake and West Kirby monument has been transformed thanks to 14 years of renovations by the Friends of Gran
evidence_packet.evidence_text: A neglected war memorial has been painstakingly restored by volunteers and lit up for the first time in its 104-year history ahead of Remembrance Day The Grade II* listed Hoylake and West Kirby monument has been transformed thanks to 14 years of renovations by the Friends of Grange Hill and Wirral Borough Council The spectacle is just one of a range of colourful tributes and events ahead of Remembrance Sunday across north-west England They include a striking display of thousands of poppies and crosses on a roundabout in Leigh, Greater Manchester, while Poulton-le-Fylde in Lancashire, has a displayed more than a 1,000 yellow poppies to honour "forgotten heroines" who served their country The Hoylake and West Kirby restoration project began in 2012 after a visitor tried to bring his father, a military veteran, to the memorial but found access virtually impossible Years of neglect had left the site overgrown while the site's remembrance garden had almost disappeared

evidence_packet.evidence_text: A guitar used by Johnny Marr after his split from The Smiths could fetch up to £30,000 when it goes under the hammer next month The white Fender American Vintage 1962 Reissue Stratocaster was played during Marr's time with British rock band The The which he joined in 1988, a year after leaving The Smiths Auctioneers Gardiner Houlgate said a private owner bought the guitar in 2020, with Marr - originally from Manchester - signing the guitar's headstock at the time and providing a handwritten postcard describing how it had been used The guitar will go on sale at the Gardiner Houlgate auction house in Corsham, Wiltshire, on 8 December where it is estimated to fetch between £20,000 and £30,000 Luke Hobbs, auctioneer at Gardiner Houlgate, said: "We're valuing this guitar at around £20,000 to £30,000 based on other recent sales of Johnny Marr's instruments "Marr's equipment is very popular with collectors and fans

evidence_packet.evidence_text: After spending more than 20 years living in caravans and motorhomes, army veteran James Makinson said having a permanent home gave him one thing: "security" Known as Jimmy, the 79-year-old was helped into accommodation in Wigan through Homes at Ease, a housing programme run by the not-for-profit organisation Armed Forces Community HQ The scheme helps veterans who are homeless or at risk of losing their homes find permanent accommodation through social housing providers and private landlords. Since 2023, it has received more than 500 referrals across the North West "I can't say enough about this place," Makinson said of Armed Forces Community HQ, which helped him Lisa Murgatroyd, strategic development director at the organisation, said 99.5% of veterans housed through the scheme remained in permanent accommodation for more than six months Murgatroyd said much of the homelessness experienced by veterans was hidden, with people staying on friends' sofas or in insecure accommodation rather than sleeping rough

evidence_packet.evidence_text: Train passengers are being warned over disruption this weekend, with direct services between Sheffield and Manchester cancelled entirely Network Rail said trains would be affected on Saturday and Sunday while work to replace the bridge deck at Beauchief, in Sheffield, is carried out Under the scheme, a new 73-tonne bridge deck, which carries the railway over the River Sheaf, will be lifted into place Ahead of the weekend's disruption, Network Rail's lead portfolio manager, Tom Grainger, said the company was "very sorry for any inconvenience" He said the work was essential to ensure the "continued safe running of the railway", adding that nearly 200ft (60m) of rail would also be renewed as part of the project As a result of the work, TransPennine Express services between Sheffield and Manchester Oxford Road via Stockport will not run this weekend, while trains between Sheffield and Manchester Piccadilly will be diverted to run via Huddersfield

evidence_packet.summary: Reform UK has insisted it supports plans for a new railway station in Bradford as part of Northern Powerhouse Rail (NPR), despite its opposition to parts of the broader project The party's deputy leader nationally, Richard Tice, said it had "never opposed" Phase 1 of NPR, which i
evidence_packet.evidence_text: Reform UK has insisted it supports plans for a new railway station in Bradford as part of Northern Powerhouse Rail (NPR), despite its opposition to parts of the broader project The party's deputy leader nationally, Richard Tice, said it had "never opposed" Phase 1 of NPR, which includes proposals for the city's new station, but remained against spending money on a high-speed line between Liverpool and Manchester However, questions remain over which parts of NPR Reform UK would support if it got into government, including a proposed new line connecting Bradford with Huddersfield and Manchester The city's Reform group say they do not believe the national stance poses a risk locally Bradford's political parties have all agreed on the importance of securing a new station as part of NPR, and specifically a through line, but opposition councillors have questioned whether the local Reform administration's commitment is shared by the party nationally At a meeting of Bradford Council's Reform-led executive earlier this week, Conservative group leader Rebecca Poulsen welcomed the proposed new station's city-centre location but said Bradford needed more than a replacement terminus

evidence_packet.evidence_text: A controversial relief road plan has been approved despite hundreds of objections The new road around Carrington in Trafford, first proposed more than a decade ago, will provide a new route to the M60 and reduce congestion in the village, the council said, as well as opening up the area for new housing About 5,000 new homes could be built on land close to Manchester United's training ground But objectors said the approval of the scheme was "heartbreaking", and it would have a devastating impact on wildlife Liz Patel, deputy leader of Trafford Council, said: "This road has been decades in the making and it will offer residents in Partington an alternative route towards the M60 "The existing road is at maximum capacity and, by our modelling, the relief road will reduce congestion in the village of Carrington by 67%, as well as opening up the area for new homes while mitigating the biodiversity along the route."

title: Developer Urban Splash forced to pay £45m over Manchester fire safety works

evidence_packet.title: Developer Urban Splash forced to pay £45m over Manchester fire safety works
evidence_packet.lead: A building developer has been ordered to pay more than £45m to the government after fire safety defects were repaired in seven high-rise buildings The buildings in Manchester, developed by Urban Splash between 2000 and 2008, were alleged to have serious defects discovered in insp
evidence_packet.summary: A building developer has been ordered to pay more than £45m to the government after fire safety defects were repaired in seven high-rise buildings The buildings in Manchester, developed by Urban Splash between 2000 and 2008, were alleged to have serious defects discovered in insp
evidence_packet.evidence_text: A building developer has been ordered to pay more than £45m to the government after fire safety defects were repaired in seven high-rise buildings The buildings in Manchester, developed by Urban Splash between 2000 and 2008, were alleged to have serious defects discovered in inspections after the Grenfell Tower disaster The extent of the defects was disputed but they have been fixed at a cost of more than £60m, with about £51.1m paid from the government's Building Safety Fund (BSF) established after the disaster The buildings were not owned by Urban Splash at the time of the remediation work and no BSF money was paid to it. A spokesperson said the scale of the liability was "significant" The Department of Housing, Communities and Local Government brought a case to a specialist tribunal, seeking an order for the developer to contribute towards the cost of the works paid from the taxpayer-supported fund On Thursday, the tribunal ruled that more than £45.7m should be paid to the government by Urban Splash

evidence_packet.evidence_text: Salford 'The only thing that works in our favour is we are all white, so we are not the obvious target' HMOs have been the targets of protest and vandalism, but they are a lifeline for some people amid spiralling rents and a shortage of social housing Add to preferred sources News Stephen Topping Senior reporter 07:20, 08 Nov 2026 For 14 years, Sean* has called Salford home. He is 32 years old and has built up a good career in the city Like thousands of people in Greater Manchester, he lives in a house in multiple occupation (HMO). It's the only way he can afford to live in the city he loves It isn't the dream, but it works for Sean. Yet earlier in October, he received an email from the property management firm that looks after the HMO, telling him and his housemates to 'be safe' The email was prompted by a wave of anger, protest and vandalism targeting properties across Salford which were alleged to be HMOs accommodating asylum seekers. 'No HMO' was daubed on doors and walls in paint, while windows were bricked across the borough in October After the spate of attacks, the property managers told Sean and his housemates to report any concerns with police, but 'not to worry'. "When something like this comes up you are going to be more aware and agitated," he told the Manchester Evening News

The officer behind the wheel of the Ford Kuga patrol car, PC Sam Lockley, was chasing a Seat Leon driven by Cameron Grainger through Rochdale The injured man spoke out as Grainger - who has a long history of motoring offences - was jailed for causing serious injury by dangerous driving at Manchester Crown Court. He lost his job and his pension after being convicted of causing serious injury by dangerous driving. evidence_packet.lead: Stockport We met on the first day of school 60 years ago, and we’re all still best mates 'It's all shake hands and hugs' View 3 Images Left to right: Anthony Ashton, Alan Murphy, Peter Wilks, Robert Reynolds, and David Platt (Image: Anthony Ashton) Add to preferred sources News L

Life as you know it is flipped on its head - and patients and their loved ones are suddenly faced with confronting appoi But just a stone's throw from the Christie Hospital, where patients face the more clinical side of cancer care, is a place that feels more like home For 10 years, Maggie's Manchester has opened its doors to anyone affected by cancer, offering a different kind of support to people impacted by the disease There's absolutely nothing clinical about its striking building, designed by world-renowned architect and Stockport-born Lord Norman Foster. evidence_packet.evidence_text: Salford 'The only thing that works in our favour is we are all white, so we are not the obvious target' HMOs have been the targets of protest and vandalism, but they are a lifeline for some people amid spiralling rents and a shortage of social housing Add to preferred sources News Stephen Topping Senior reporter 07:20, 08 Nov 2026 For 14 years, Sean* has called Salford home. He is 32 years old and has built up a good career in the city Like thousands of people in Greater Manchester, he lives in a house in multiple occupation (HMO). It's the only way he can afford to live in the city he loves It isn't the dream, but it works for Sean. Yet earlier in October, he received an email from the property management firm that looks after the HMO, telling him and his housemates to 'be safe' The email was prompted by a wave of anger, protest and vandalism targeting properties across Salford which were alleged to be HMOs accommodating asylum seekers. 'No HMO' was daubed on doors and walls in paint, while windows were bricked across the borough in October After the spate of attacks, the property managers told Sean and his housemates to report any concerns with police, but 'not to worry'. "When something like this comes up you are going to be more aware and agitated," he told the Manchester Evening News

evidence_packet.evidence_text: Greater Manchester Combined Authority Greater Manchester Combined Authority gave nearly £1m to anonymous figures in ‘secret’ payments A Manchester Evening News investigation has revealed that the Greater Manchester Combined Authority handed nearly £1m Add to preferred sources News Declan Carey Local Democracy Reporter 07:20, 08 Nov 2026 The Greater Manchester Combined Authority (GMCA) has given nearly £1m to anonymous beneficiaries since 2024 in a series of ‘secret’ payments The payments are listed in the GMCA’s public accounts to pay for consultancy work, professional fees, commissioned services, grants, and other things, but there is little detail on what specific services were provided and who the money went to A spokesperson for the GMCA said it redacts details of named individuals who receive payments when their name is not their trading name, which it said is 'in line with UK data protection legislation and local government transparency code of practice.' It added that its system is under 'continual review' The combined authority is facing calls for more transparency around where it is spending public money and what services were provided for the cash

The officer behind the wheel of the Ford Kuga patrol car, PC Sam Lockley, was chasing a Seat Leon driven by Cameron Grainger through Rochdale The injured man spoke out as Grainger - who has a long history of motoring offences - was jailed for causing serious injury by dangerous driving at Manchester Crown Court. He said he blames the 25-year-old, even though it wasn't his car that hit him PC Lockley was handed a suspended prison sentence in February. He lost his job and his pension after being convicted of causing serious injury by dangerous driving. PC Lockley was also ordered to carry out 15 days of community service and banned from the road for two years The 41-year-old victim - a father-of-one and a forklift truck driver originally from Poland - described the devastating impact the crash has had on his life, leading to lifelong injuries and the breakdown of his family life

Credit: UK Parliament A Labour MP has revealed that she is a victim of domestic abuse - Speaking in the Commons on October 13, Kirith Entwistle, who represents Bolton North East, described her experience of the current court system as "triggering", adding that she had to watch her abuser "stare at her" during a recent video hearing Ms Entwistle told her fellow MPs that she believes special measures - where victims are given protection or assistance in court - should be the standard in cases involving domestic abuse Examples of these measures could include screens, the ability to give evidence through a live link, or witnesses being able to be accompanied when giving evidence Measures to protect victims are included in the Courts and Tribunals Bill, which is currently going through Parliament Speaking during a debate on the bill, Ms Entwistle said: "It doesn’t matter how many times somebody tells me that they understand what I’m going through, or they acknowledge what I’ve been through, they really don’t unless they have lived it themselves or know somebody who has."

evidence_packet.evidence_text: Police across Greater Manchester made 17 arrests last nightas part of Operation Treacle, the response to anti-social behaviour linked to fireworks and Bonfire Night Throughout the evening, officers used dispersal powers to prevent further disorder, seized fireworks, and carried out targeted patrols in identified hotspot locations These proactive tactics will continue throughout the Bonfire Night period, alongside engagement with local communities, local authorities and partner agencies The arrests made last night are all linked to anti-social behaviour and the misuse of fireworks, either through incidents reported by members of the public or offences identified proactively by neighbourhood officers on patrol with the support of response officers and officers fr Of the 17 arrests made across Greater Manchester, eight were in Tameside after receiving reports of youths using fireworks in Millennium Green Park in Ashton-Under-Lyne, they were tracked by our drone’s unit and arrested in a nearby shop on suspicion of affray Officer across Greater Manchester also conducted over 160 stop and searches and seized over 600 fireworks, demonstrating the force’s continued commitment to tackling behaviour that causes harm, fear and disruption within our communities

evidence_packet.evidence_text: Bruntwood and Bury Council, through their joint venture partnership, are inviting local people, businesses and traders to help shape proposals for the first phase of Mill Gate’s redevelopment The public consultation runs from Monday 9th – Sunday 29th November, giving people the opportunity to view the proposals and share their feedback ahead of a planning application being submitted in December. The proposals focus on opening up the town centre and making it easier to At the heart of the plans is a new public square, alongside improved pedestrian routes linking Mill Gate with Bury Market, new community destination Casewells, the Interchange and the wider town centre. Landscaping, planting and seating would create a welcoming place to meet and Proposals for Minden and Market Parade include removing vehicle access to create a more welcoming pedestrian route and public space, with trees, planting and seating The proposed relocation of the Mill Gate multi-storey car park entrance and exit to Angouleme Way would help open up space behind the car park for an improved pedestrian route and landscaping, while maintaining servicing arrangements for retailers and the market Upgraded shopfronts, modernised canopies, high-quality paving and better lighting would create a more welcoming environment and help people feel safer when visiting after dark

evidence_packet.evidence_text: Experience the raw, unfiltered power of Balkan folklore in a new immersive show from the world’s most famous performance artist Balkan Erotic Epic is a bold new performance work created by the iconic artist Marina Abramović . Regarded as the world’s most influential performance artist, Abramović’s transformative work has reached millions of people – from opening the Pyramid Stage at Glastonbury Festival t A four-hour ritual where ancient myth meets performance art, Balkan Erotic Epic explores the eroticism, spirituality and traditions of Abramović’s homeland through 13 visceral scenes Brought to life by a cast of over 70 performers, dancers, musicians and singers, the experience unfolds across Aviva Studios. Audiences are free to choose their own path – with pop-up encounters punctuating the action, bringing bodies together in dance, song and ritual Watch Fertility Rite , a fevered ritual where bodies writhe against the ground in a desperate call for fertility. Witness Massaging the Breast where women gesticulate over graves to awaken the earth. In Scaring the Gods , women bare themselves to the sky to banish storms. Listen Unafraid to push the boundaries of eroticism and performance art, Balkan Erotic Epic asks its audience a timeless question: What are our bodies truly for?

Sun 08 Nov 2026 12:00PM Aldridge Studio Tickets Sun 08 Nov 2026 3:00PM Aldridge Studio Tickets There is only one word used in our show - it’s ‘Hay!’ Like the stuffing in Geenie’s scarecrow, ‘Hay!’ like the sound she makes when he comes to life and ‘Hay!’ when he sees all the wonders of the natural world for the first time. Only one word but so many meanings in a show about growing up in the heart of the countryside and discovering that you don’t have to stay stuck in the mud – you can live your dreams, spread your wings and fly like the birds. A highly accessible show filled with music, clowning, song and dance. In this beautiful story Farmer Geenie guides scarecrow step by step as he finds his feet, then his hands, his voice, his legs and his love of song and dance in a story about the fun of growing up where everyday there’s something new to make you say ‘Hay!’ Our two very talented physical theatre performers are expert clowns and so our show doesn’t use any words – everything is told in a fantastically clear way through sound, dance, music and our incredibly inventive props which playfully represent the essential elements of nature that this show celebrates. We’ve got charming puppets – the birds of course and also the butterflies and bees - and some very wonderful eggs each with their own particular surprises. All of this means that our show is highly accessible and perfect for a younger age-group who will be giggling all the way through this gentle introduction to what theatre can be - sweet, funny, inclusive and uplifting. evidence_packet.evidence_text: Wednesday 12 May 2027 – Band on the Wall Thursday 13 May 2027 – Southbank Centre Sona Jobarteh is the first professional female kora virtuoso to emerge from any of West Africa’s five Griot dynasties, and a singer, composer and bandleader whose concerts fill some of the world’s finest halls. In 2026 she sold out the Elbphilharmonie in Hamburg, played Munich’s Prinzregententheater and the Schleswig-Holstein Musik Festival, and on October 11 received the Silicon Valley African Film Festival’s 2026 Icon Award for her contributions to African music, scholarship and cultural promotion. On stage, Sona sings and plays the 21-string kora and guitar, joined by Eric Appapoulay, also on guitar, Andi McLean on bass, Yuval Wetzler on drums, Anselmo Neto on percussion and her son, Sidiki Jobarteh, on balafon. The show blends Mandé griot tradition with blues, Afropop and contemporary songwriting. She has also toured with blues legend Taj Mahal. Her concerts have become events wherever she plays. She has performed more than a hundred shows across Europe, Africa, the United States and beyond, in some of the world’s most prestigious theaters and festivals, with sell-outs at London’s Barbican, Cologne’s Philharmonie and the Seine Musicale in Paris, and appearances at the Hollywood Bowl, Symphony Space in New York and WOMAD Australia and New Zealand. Her latest album, Badinyaa Kumoo, was named one of the best albums of its year by Songlines Magazine, and her single “Gambia” has passed 32 million YouTube views. Recent collaborations include a feature on LL Cool J’s album The FORCE, on the song “Black Code Suite”, and a guest appearance on “Se a Vida Pede” from the Brazilian group Gilsons’ latest album. evidence_packet.evidence_text: Finish work and unwind with live music from Manchester’s best jazz musicians. Beat the Jams live series showcases the very best of the jazz scene, at short rush hour gigs from 6pm at Band on the Wall. What better way to avoid those endless queues, chaotic traffic and stressful homeward journeys? Clock off and skip the rush-hour traffic while you watch live jazz and make the most of our happy hour deals from 5–7pm: £4.50 pints / 2 for £15 cocktails / £15 bottles of wine + pizzas from £5! The new season kicks off on 24 September with tenor saxophonist Dean Masser and pianist Richard Wetherall, followed by: 7 October – Anna Chandler-King Quartet Leeds based saxophonist and composer Anna joins us again for Beat the Jams, this time with her own band. Anna’s thoughtful and inventive compositions are firm favourites of us at Beat the Jams and her quartet promises to be a unique rush hour busting treat! 16 November – Sam Lightwing Quartet Saxophonist and composer Sam Lightwing brings presents brand new music for his thrilling young quartet, showcasing Sam’s original compositions, which blend classic mainstream jazz grooves with modern flavours of post-pop and latin, all wrapped up in the language of contemporary sax giants such as Chris Potter, Seamus Blake and Joshua Redman. 15 December – Svarc/Devine/Walsh with Richard Iles The band combines deep pocket, fearless interplay and a shared love of exploration. Expect everything from soulful melodies and infectious rhythms to moments of exhilarating collective improvisation, delivered with the chemistry that only world-class musicians can create. Tickets from £13 per show, or £42 for a season ticket

evidence_packet.lead: We’re inviting young people to explore music for film and compose their own soundtrack this summer!
evidence_packet.summary: We’re inviting young people to explore music for film and compose their own soundtrack this summer! […] The post Young Musician’s Summer School appeared first on Band on the Wall
evidence_packet.evidence_text: We’re inviting young people to explore music for film and compose their own soundtrack this summer! Whether your child already attends our Saturday Music Club, or just wants to try something new, our Young Musician’s Summer School is suitable for all abilities! Across this 5 day course, we’ll be exploring music for film, and working on composing music for the silent film ‘A Trip to the Moon’. The course will conclude with a live performance soundtracking the film for family and friends. We welcome all abilities and instruments to take part in this course. evidence_packet.evidence_text: Mr Thomas’s Chop House has been part of Manchester since 1867. A £300,000 restoration, long-term lease and 23-year-old head chef are shaping what comes next Go to Manchester's Finest X profile Mr Thomas’s Chop House has been serving Manchester since 1867, but owner Roger Ward admits there was a point after Covid when he wasn’t sure how much longer he wanted to keep doing it Tom’s had gone eight years without a proper lease and much longer without any meaningful investment by the landlord. Retirement was being seriously considered. Instead, Roger decided to “go again properly” That decision has resulted in a new long-term commitment to the Chop Houses and around £300,000 being spent restoring Tom’s – touching everything from the dining rooms and furniture to the menu, wine list, kitchen and beer cellars Roger is particularly pleased with the toilets “Tom’s was famous for the shittest toilets in town,” he says. They are now, by his assessment, considerably less so. Downstairs has been redone, upstairs has new ones too, while a previously overlooked back room has been completely reworked

evidence_packet.lead: The government's new Digital and Technologies Jobs Plan aims to create 200,000 entry-level jobs over the next decade, recognising the barriers facing employers and the importance of regional organisations in connecting people with opportunities.
evidence_packet.summary: The government's new Digital and Technologies Jobs Plan aims to create 200,000 entry-level jobs over the next decade, recognising the barriers facing employers and the importance of regional organisations in connecting people with opportunities. The government has published its D
evidence_packet.evidence_text: The government's new Digital and Technologies Jobs Plan aims to create 200,000 entry-level jobs over the next decade, recognising the barriers facing employers and the importance of regional organisations in connecting people with opportunities. The government has published its D The plan acknowledges that the challenge is not simply a shortage of people with digital skills. Entry-level recruitment has become more difficult, with employers increasingly favouring experienced candidates and many graduates and other new entrants struggling to secure their fi Manchester Digital contributed to the development of the plan through its involvement in the government's Digital Skills Council, drawing on its work with employers and education providers across Greater Manchester Around 800,000 digital and technology roles are projected to need filling over the next decade. The plan sets out an ambition to create 200,000 entry-level jobs, including apprenticeships, during that period The plan also addresses how AI is changing workforce requirements and the importance of ensuring people entering the industry have both technical knowledge and practical workplace skills Manchester Digital's 2026 Sector Insights Report highlighted a reduction of around 20% in early-career opportunities, despite continued demand for experienced technology professionals

evidence_packet.evidence_text: L-R: Simon Shaw, Anna Dick, Alastair Brown, Tripti Anil, Alan Jackson Simon Shaw, Delivery Director at Codurance, hosted the lunchtime session for tech leaders and introduced Codurance, which is a global software engineering consultancy that has run its Manchester office for 15 years He was joined on the panel by Anna Dick, Chief Technology & Product Officer at Capsule; Alastair Brown, Group Director of AI and Technology at Peninsula; Tripti Anil, Senior Leader, Data & Analytics at Kellanova; and Alan Jackson, Director of Client Solutions at Codurance Talking about discovering how AI can be used in projects, Anna said that Capsule's initial three months of AI exploration across all its business teams built appetite for further experimentation, but it also got a little out of control. Some things needed revisiting and tidying u Alastair stressed product discipline in order to understand the business driver and the outcome you want. At Peninsula, one initiative focused on giving customers richer answers and delivered over £1m in revenue. He said success depends on strong sponsorship and expertise from wi Tripti described spending three years building data foundations at Kellanova, focusing on "the right things at the right time" and bringing business teams along on the journey. They started with UK field sales as a proof of concept initially

That depends who you ask… Tech by Chris Newbould November 4, 2026 Lecturers and students have significantly different perceptions of how much generative artificial intelligence (AI) is being used in university studies, according to new research from The University of Manchester and Spain’s Universidad del Pais Vasco/Euskal Herriko Unibertsitatea. The study found that academic staff perceived students to be using AI tools such as ChatGPT for their studies much more extensively than students reported themselves. Researchers say the findings highlight a gap in understanding between staff and students, at a time when universities are grappling with how best to respond to the technology. Academic staff rated their perception of students’ AI use at 5.23 out of seven, compared with an average of 3.11 among students reporting their own use for academic purposes. READ MORE: ANS Group reports 500% RoI from latest AI deployment Students were more positive than staff about the potential benefits of generative AI, including its ability to improve productivity, support learning and reduce workloads. The most prominent uses reported by students involved producing written text, finding answers to assignments, and translating or improving grammar. Staff varied considerably in their experience and expertise with AI, making it difficult for some to judge how students were using the technology. Crediflow AI has developed a platform that pulls together the information credit teams currently gather and process by hand, such as financial statements, bank transactions and borrower documents, and turns it into structured credit analysis. The company uses AI to automate much of that work, which is typically spread across spreadsheets, PDFs, emails and other disconnected systems. Aggregating this data manually can sometimes take up to several days, but Crediflow says its platform reduces that time to between 10 and 30 minutes, giving credit teams more time to concentrate on critical tasks. READ MORE: Leeds financial tech consultancy merges with London cloud specialist In practice, the platform extracts and standardises figures from a borrower’s accounts, a process the industry calls financial spreading, analyses cash flow and drafts the memo a lender’s credit committee uses to approve a loan, in each customer’s preferred format. It runs every Sunday from February right through to December, drawing over 300 sellers and t
evidence_packet.evidence_text: Bolton Car Boot Sale is one of the North West's biggest weekly boot sales, held in the hardstanding car park of the Macron Stadium (formerly Reebok), Burnden Way, Horwich, Bolton BL6 6JW. It runs every Sunday from February right through to December, drawing over 300 sellers and thousands of bargain hunters each week. Sellers can arrive and set up from 6:00 AM, with buyers welcomed in from 7:00 AM. Entry costs just £1 per car for buyers. Pitches for sellers are £14 for a car, £20 for a van and £3 for a trailer, with regular and corner pitches available on request. Bring exact change to keep the queue moving, and call organiser Andrew on 07470784644 for more details. Expect hundreds of stalls across the concrete hardstanding pitches, so it goes ahead in most weather.
